item.title: Webster County Health Department to remain closed through April for renovations - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Morgan Howard
item.description:
WEBSTER COUNTY – The Webster County Health Department will remain closed through the month of April as remodeling work continues, according to the Mississippi State Department of Health.

Health officials said phone calls to the Webster County office will continue to be transferred to the Calhoun County Health Department during the closure.

Residents can contact the Calhoun County Health Department at 662-412-3260 for assistance while the Webster County office remains closed.

The state health department said the temporary closure is part of ongoing improvements aimed at better serving the community.

Officials encouraged residents to check the MSDH Healthy Mobile App and the agency’s website for updates.

item.title: Tupelo police, Crime Stoppers seek suspects in multiple credit card fraud cases - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Morgan Howard
item.description:
TUPELO – Crime Stoppers of Northeast Mississippi and the Tupelo Police Department are asking for the public’s help in identifying the people involved in multiple credit card fraud cases reported in and around Tupelo.

Crimestoppers said the cases happened March 13.

Investigators released photos of the suspects and are urging anyone who recognizes them or has information about the incidents to come forward.

Anyone with information is asked to call Crime Stoppers of Northeast Mississippi at 800-773-TIPS or submit an anonymous tip through the P3 Tips app.

Crime Stoppers said it is offering up to $2,000 in cash for information that leads to an arrest. Officials said tipsters can remain anonymous.

item.title: Shilo Sanders highlights JSU's 2026 P.R.O.M. Promise event - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Special to Darkhorse Press
item.description:
By Anthony Howard Jackson State University

Jackson — Jackson State University hosted its 2026 P.R.O.M. Promise event, welcoming hundreds of high school students from the Jackson Public School District (JPS) for a day focused on empowerment, education and life preparation. This year’s event was highlighted by a special appearance from Shilo Sanders, whose message resonated strongly with attendees. Sanders, known for his leadership both on and off the field, shared personal insights on discipline, accountability and making positive life choices.

“Your decisions today shape your future,” Sanders told students. “Stay focused, surround yourself with the right people, and always remember your goals.”

The P.R.O.M. Promise—Please Return On Monday—is a signature initiative created by JSU’s Metro Jackson Community Prevention Coalition (MJCPC) designed to guide students in making informed, responsible decisions during prom season and beyond. The program addresses critical topics such as personal safety, peer pressure, mental and physical health, and post-secondary planning.

According to the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA), distracted driving, especially texting or using social media while driving, is common among younger drivers. Statistics gathered by NHTSA documented that 3,275 people were killed in distraction-related crashes in 2023; 241 were teens, 15 to 19 years old.

“We started this initiative about 18 years ago. It started with small groups and has grown to this big event,” said Henry Thompson, director and principal investigator of MJCPC. “We’re trying to make sure these students return home safely without drinking and driving.”

Held on JSU’s campus, the event featured a rollover crash demonstration by the Mississippi Department of Transportation, a Q&A session with Sanders and a motivational speech from speaker Dwight Owens.

The high school students were also surprised by a live performance from Baton Rouge, Louisiana-based rapper H3adband. He performed his viral TikTok hit, “Boo,” which is currently on the Billboard Hot 100.

MJCPC emphasized that P.R.O.M. Promise is about preparing students for prom night and equipping them with tools for lifelong success. The program continues to grow each year, reinforcing JSU’s leadership in outreach and mentorship.

item.title: Rankin County Animal Shelter launches half-off adoption event as kennels fill up - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Morgan Howard
item.description:
RANKIN COUNTY – The Rankin County Animal Shelter is asking the public to adopt as it faces overcrowding and runs out of available kennel space.

Shelter officials said the facility is over capacity again and currently has no free kennels.

To help more pets find homes, the shelter is holding a half-off adoption event Friday and Saturday, March 27 and 28.

During the event, dog adoption fees will be reduced to $65. The fee includes spay or neuter services, a rabies vaccine, core vaccinations and a microchip, according to the shelter. Adopters also will receive a free collar and leash.

Shelter officials said the first eight adopters who take part in the special will also receive a gift card from The Cleaners by Pizza Shack.

The shelter is located at 710 Marquette Road in Brandon.

Officials encouraged people who cannot adopt to share the shelter’s message to help more animals find homes.

item.title: Mississippi wildlife officials conduct annual deer herd health evaluations across state - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Morgan Howard
item.description:
JACKSON – Wildlife biologists in Mississippi have spent the past several weeks conducting annual deer herd health evaluations across the state to monitor reproduction, body condition and disease prevalence in mature female deer.

The Mississippi Department of Wildlife, Fisheries and Parks said the evaluations are being carried out in partnership with the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service and Mississippi State University.

Officials said the surveys focus on female deer ages 2.5 years and older and are conducted each year on wildlife management areas, state parks, U.S. military lands and other public and private properties.

According to the department, the evaluations are especially important in areas where updated breeding data is needed, hunting pressure is limited, or herd changes are being monitored.

During the evaluations, biologists collect breeding data to determine peak rut timing, disease data including parasite loads and testing for epizootic hemorrhagic disease and chronic wasting disease, and body condition data such as weight and Kidney Fat Index.

Officials said the information helps track deer herd health over time and identify potential concerns, including low body weights or high parasite loads.

The department said all deer harvested during the evaluations are donated to charitable organizations, including Hunters for the Hungry and local food banks.

item.title: Mayor John Horhn Expresses Appreciation to Sheriff Tyree Jones - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Special to Darkhorse Press
item.description:
Statement from Mayor John Horhn on the service of Sheriff Tyree Jones as Jackson Police Chief:

I want to extend my thanks to Sheriff Tyree Jones for stepping up to lead the Jackson Police Department during an important time for our city. His leadership and understanding of both community needs and law enforcement helped ensure a smooth transition while we worked to identify our next chief.

I’m grateful for his willingness to take on this added responsibility in service to the people of Jackson. I look forward to our continued collaboration as we move forward working together.

We now welcome Dr. RaShall Brackney as our new Chief of Police. Her experience and strong record of leadership will bring valuable perspective to the department and further the city’s goals of safety, accountability, and community trust.

Thank you.

item.title: Madison County deputies seek public’s help in locating armed suspect - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Therese Apel
item.description:
MADISON COUNTY — The Madison County Sheriff’s Office is asking for the public’s help in locating a man wanted in connection with an aggravated assault involving a shooting, authorities said.

Antonio Harris, 31, is wanted after allegedly shooting a victim with a handgun, according to investigators. Deputies described Harris as a Black male, approximately 6 feet 2 inches tall and weighing about 200 pounds. He should be considered armed and dangerous.

Officials urged residents not to approach Harris and to contact law enforcement immediately with any information about his whereabouts.

Authorities said a reward of up to $2,500 may be available for information leading to Harris’ arrest. Tips can be submitted by calling Crime Stoppers at 601-355-TIPS (8477) or online through its tip submission service.

No additional details about the shooting or the victim were immediately released. The investigation remains ongoing.

item.title: Dangerous gas leak forces closure of Bristol Crossing in Flowood - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Morgan Howard
item.description:
FLOWOOD – Bristol Crossing in Flowood has been completely shut down because of a gas leak, according to the Flowood Police Department.

Police said the combustion level in the area is dangerously high, and no vehicle or foot traffic is being allowed through the area.

Authorities said the school district has been notified so buses can use alternate routes for after-school drop-offs nearby.

Police said the estimated time for the road to reopen is 7 p.m.

item.title: Court affirms two life sentences for Biloxi man convicted of sexually abusing stepdaughters - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Therese Apel
item.description:
JACKSON — The Mississippi Court of Appeals on Tuesday upheld the conviction and two life sentences of a Biloxi man found guilty of repeatedly sexually abusing his two stepdaughters over several years.

In a unanimous decision, the court affirmed the 2024 Harrison County Circuit Court verdict against John Nathaniel Pierre, who was convicted on 14 counts of sexual battery and one count of attempted sexual battery involving the girls, who were minors at the time of the abuse.

According to the opinion, Pierre lived with his wife and her daughters from 2016 until 2021. The abuse came to light in August 2022, when the older daughter confronted Pierre, recorded the conversation, and disclosed the allegations to her mother. Pierre fled when confronted but was later arrested after leading officers on a high‑speed chase that reached more than 120 mph.

At trial, both victims testified that Pierre forced sexual acts on them beginning when they were as young as five.

Pierre appealed, arguing that a jury instruction improperly emphasized the victims’ testimony and that the evidence was insufficient to prove penetration in several counts. The Court of Appeals rejected both claims, noting that the defense failed to properly object to the instruction at trial and that Mississippi law requires only “slight penetration” to sustain a sexual battery conviction.

The court found the younger victim’s testimony sufficient for a reasonable jury to conclude penetration occurred.

Pierre is serving two consecutive life sentences in the custody of the Mississippi Department of Corrections.

item.title: Copiah Animal Shelter urgently needs foster homes as kennels reach capacity - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Morgan Howard
item.description:
COPIAH COUNTY- The Copiah Animal Shelter is asking the public to step up as the shelter reaches full capacity and runs out of space for dogs and puppies in need.

Shelter officials said they urgently need foster homes to help relieve overcrowding and give animals a safe, temporary place to stay.

According to the shelter, some of the dogs are experiencing stress in the kennel environment, while others are recovering and need a quieter place to heal.

Officials said fostering can make a major difference by opening up space and giving more animals a chance to be rescued and cared for.

The shelter provides food, veterinary care and supplies for foster animals, while foster families provide a temporary home and daily care.

Officials said even fostering one dog for a few days or a couple of weeks can help save additional lives.

Anyone interested in fostering is asked to message the shelter or call 601-954-6447. The shelter is located in Crystal Springs.

item.title: Canadian Fugitive Wanted for Murder Indicted on Federal Charges in Mississippi - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Therese Apel
item.description:
OXFORD — A Canadian fugitive wanted for murder in Toronto has been indicted on federal firearms and immigration charges after his arrest earlier this week in north Mississippi, U.S. Attorney Scott F. Leary announced.

Adrian Walker, 28, a Canadian national, is charged with illegal entry into the United States and being an illegal alien in possession of a firearm. The charges follow his arrest Monday in Tupelo.

Authorities said Walker was wanted by the Toronto Police Service on a nationwide warrant for first-degree murder and attempted murder stemming from a May 7, 2024, shooting in Toronto. He had been listed as a “Most Wanted Person.”

Walker was taken into custody in Lee County by agents with the U.S. Marshals Service, including its Gulf Coast Regional Fugitive Task Force, along with U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement Homeland Security Investigations and the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives. He was initially arrested on an immigration violation warrant.

“As previously stated, this was a serious case,” Leary said in a statement. “A Canadian national, wanted for murder, entered our country illegally and was living in our midst.”

Leary added that the case underscores the risks law enforcement officers face and praised the agencies involved in the arrest.

The case is being prosecuted by Assistant U.S. Attorneys Clyde McGee and John Herzog Jr.

Officials said the investigation is part of a Homeland Security Task Force effort under Operation Take Back America, a federal initiative targeting illegal immigration and transnational criminal organizations.

item.title: Brandon man convicted on multiple child sex charges - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Therese Apel
item.description:
RANKIN COUNTY — A Brandon man was found guilty on multiple charges involving the sexual abuse of a child following a trial in Rankin County Circuit Court, District Attorney John K. Bramlett announced.

Mark Duett, 60, was convicted on three counts of sexual battery and two counts of gratification of lust, all involving a child. A judge has scheduled sentencing for May 11.

The case began March 14, 2025, when officers with the Brandon Police Department responded to a 911 call reporting abuse of a young child. During the investigation, the child was taken to a Children’s Advocacy Center, where the child disclosed that the abuse occurred over a three-month period and involved multiple incidents of sexual contact when the defendant was alone with the child.

Authorities later executed a search warrant at Duett’s residence, where investigators collected electronic devices and other evidence related to the case.

Prosecutors presented testimony from law enforcement officers, an investigator, a sexual assault nurse, a forensic interviewer from the Children’s Advocacy Center and other witnesses, along with evidence gathered during the investigation.

“This was calculated, repeated abuse of a child,” Bramlett said in a statement. “The jury saw it for what it was, and the result is a conviction on every count. If you prey on children in Rankin County, we will find you, we will prosecute you, and we will make sure you are removed from this community.”

The district attorney’s office credited the Brandon Police Department, the Children’s Advocacy Center and the Center for Violence Prevention for their work on the case. Assistant District Attorneys Kathryn Newman and Amanda Fritz prosecuted the case.

item.title: Blue Angels land at NAS Meridian ahead of Wings Over Meridian Air Show - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Cash Matlock
item.description:
MERIDIAN – The U.S. Navy Blue Angels arrived Thursday morning, March 26, at Naval Air Station Meridian ahead of the Wings Over Meridian Air Show this weekend, March 28 and 29.

Queen City Newsfeed was on hand to watch the team land and speak with members of the squadron as they arrived in Meridian for the show, which is free and open to the public.

For Capt. Adam Bryan, Blue Angel No. 1 and commanding officer and flight leader of the United States Navy Flight Demonstration Squadron, the visit marks his first time in Meridian.

Bryan, who has served in the Navy for more than 20 years, is in his second year with the Blue Angels. He said this season will be his last with the team.

“As the commanding officer and flight leader, I’m first and foremost in charge with the safety and well-being of the team,” Bryan said.

“I have the honor and the opportunity to lead around the formation out here that you’re going to see both Saturday and Sunday,” he said.

Bryan said the Blue Angels perform at about 32 show sites each season and conduct roughly 65 flight demonstrations.

“There is no room for error, but that makes us concentrate even more,” Bryan said.

During the performance, he said, the precision is extreme.

“We’ll be about 12-18 inches apart from wing tip to wing tip,” Bryan said.

The Blue Angels’ arrival also spotlighted the extensive work required behind the scenes to keep the aircraft ready for flight.

“A lot of maintenance goes into keeping up these aircraft, but it’s really the pilots that make the show go on. We just try to keep the jets up so these pilots can fly in the show,” said Kayleigh Temple, an aviation structural mechanic.

Maj. Scott Laux, Blue Angel No. 6, said landing in a place with deep ties to naval aviation makes the visit especially meaningful.

“It’s really cool. It’s awesome to be somewhere that is such a part of Naval Aviation,” Laux said. “Half of our strike fighter aviators get their wings here at Meridian. It’s a place that a lot of us have passed through and trained, and on the enlisted side as well, there’s multiple school houses here where our enlisted folks have trained, so again, it’s always special when you get to go somewhere that is so important to Naval aviation and is a home for so many people.”

Laux said the team spent months preparing for the demonstration season.

“We had around 140 training flights around Naval Air Facility El Centro and NAS Pensacola as well, getting ready for the show season, refining some stuff to be able to take this product in front of the crowd,” he said.

He said the team hopes the show inspires people in Meridian, whether or not they choose a military path.

“Obviously we’re out here representing the Navy and the Marine Corps, obviously there’s a Naval Air Station here that’s important to this community, but even if folks don’t want to join the service, just be excellent at whatever you do,” Laux said. “That can start all the way as a child, all the way into later in life, so be excellent at what you do, and we hope to showcase some of that out here for the folks this weekend.”

The Wings Over Meridian Air Show will take place Saturday and Sunday at NAS Meridian. More information on attending is available at the event website.

item.title: Adams County fugitive captured in Baton Rouge - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Morgan Howard
item.description:
ADAMS COUNTY – One of Adams County’s most wanted fugitives was captured Thursday in Baton Rouge, Louisiana, according to the Adams County Sheriff’s Office.

item.title: Texas Man Sentenced to 34 Years for Cocaine Trafficking in Rankin County - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Therese Apel
item.description:
RANKIN COUNTY — A Texas man has been sentenced to 34 years in prison after a Rankin County jury found him guilty of aggravated trafficking of cocaine, District Attorney Bubba Bramlett announced.

Jorge Rodriguez, 36, of El Paso, Texas, was convicted following a trial in Rankin County Circuit Court. He was ordered to serve the sentence day-for-day in the custody of the Mississippi Department of Corrections without the possibility of parole.

The conviction stems from a traffic stop on Interstate 20 conducted by the Rankin County Sheriff’s Department Criminal Interdiction Unit. During the stop, deputies, assisted by a K-9 unit, discovered approximately 12 kilograms of cocaine concealed in the trunk of the vehicle Rodriguez was occupying.

Authorities said the drugs were hidden inside a tire that did not belong to the vehicle.

Prosecutors also presented testimony from a special agent with the Texas Department of Public Safety, who said Rodriguez sold him four ounces of cocaine roughly two months before the Rankin County arrest while the agent was working undercover.

“This was not a small amount of drugs or a close call — this was large-scale trafficking,” Bramlett said in a statement. “When that kind of activity comes through Rankin County, we will find it, we will prosecute it, and we will make sure those responsible face serious time.”

The district attorney’s office credited the Rankin County Sheriff’s Department, the Texas Department of Public Safety and the Mississippi Forensics Laboratory for their roles in the investigation and prosecution.

item.title: Taste of Mississippi Returns April 13 to Benefit Stewpot Community Services - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Therese Apel
item.description:
JACKSON — The annual Taste of Mississippi will return April 13, bringing together dozens of local restaurants, live music and community support for a longtime Jackson nonprofit.

Now in its 37th year, the event will be held from 7 to 10 p.m. at the Mississippi Trade Mart, offering both indoor and outdoor experiences. Organizers say the event will take place rain or shine.

Guests will sample food from more than 30 participating restaurants while voting for awards including Best Appetizer, Best Entrée, Best Dessert, Best Presentation and People’s Choice. Live entertainment will be provided by Aa’Keela & The Beats and The Lonely Hearts Duo.

Proceeds from the event benefit Stewpot Community Services, which provides free food, clothing and shelter to those in need. Funds raised also support the organization’s shelters, food pantry, street outreach, after-school programs and daily noon meal service.

Organizers say the event has grown over the years with support from local businesses, sponsors and attendees, raising more than $100,000 annually.

“This event is about more than great food — it’s about giving back to our community,” organizers said in a release.

Tickets are $55 for general admission, which includes unlimited tastings, and $90 for a Tasting Plus option that includes four drink tickets. The event is open to those 21 and older.

Tickets and additional information are available at stewpot.org/tasteofms.

NATCHEZ — A fundraiser has been launched to help cover funeral expenses for a Natchez man who was killed Sunday night after being struck by a vehicle along U.S. Highway 61.

“He was unfortunately struck by a vehicle … and passed on, and I can really use the help to get him cremated,” he wrote. “I thank you for taking the time to read this.”

The crash remains under investigation by the Mississippi Highway Patrol.

item.author: Morgan Howard
item.description:
TUPELO – A former Tupelo neurologist was sentenced Tuesday to 15 years in prison after pleading guilty to possession of child pornography, according to the district attorney’s office.

Ali Ahmad entered the guilty plea March 24 in state court. Senior Circuit Court Judge Paul S. Funderburk sentenced him to 15 years in the custody of the Mississippi Department of Corrections.

Because of the nature of the offense, Ahmad is not eligible for parole and must serve the sentence day for day, officials said.

Ahmad also was sentenced earlier this year in federal court. On Feb. 11, Chief U.S. District Judge Debra M. Brown sentenced him to 144 months in prison on a charge of distribution of child pornography, along with five years of supervised release and $96,100 in restitution to the victims of the offense.

Officials said the 15-year state sentence will run concurrently with the federal sentence.

According to the U.S. Attorney’s Office for the Northern District of Mississippi, Ahmad’s work visa has been revoked and he will be deported after serving his sentence.

item.title: Register now for the 2026 PowWow women's training weekend at Boondocks Firearms Training Academy - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Therese Apel
item.description:
RAYMOND — Boondocks Firearms Training Academy is working on lining up top-notch speakers and training for the 2026 PowWow, to be held April 17-18, 2026 .

The PowWow is an annual weekend of hands-on firearm training and community-building exclusively for women. The event aims to provide participants with exposure to industry-leading instructors, product demonstrations, and a supportive environment for skill development.

In the past, training sessions have included room clearing, carjacking avoidance, hand-to-hand self-defense, “shoot or don’t shoot,” and competitive shooting among others. Instructors are a combination of Boondocks staff instructors and experts from all over the country. There are also legal experts who often offer availability to answer questions about use of force in self-defense, and firearms instructors provide one-on-one interaction to help each participant learn something they didn’t know before they got there.

Through the years, the event has grown and built a group of women who have connected with each other from around the country. Some have come with friends or with sisters or mothers or daughters, and some come alone. But all leave with invaluable relationships.

Boondocks FTA “Pow Wow” is always unforgettable, invaluable – Darkhorse Press

The Pow Wow will kick off on Friday, April 17, with a registration and welcome reception from 6:00 to 9:00 p.m., featuring guest speakers and heavy hors d’oeuvres. Saturday, April 18, will be dedicated to training sessions, with four 90-minute classes covering various aspects of firearm safety and handling. Breakfast and lunch will be provided, and the day will conclude with a dinner under the stars, complete with music and entertainment. The event will wrap up with a giveaway and closing remarks from 7:00 to 8:30 p.m.

To ensure adequate planning for speakers and classes, Boondocks FTA encourages interested participants to register in advance. Registration can be completed here or by visiting boondocksfta.com and selecting the green date on the April 2026 calendar to access the registration form.

For more information or assistance, contact Boondocks FTA at (769) 972-2382 or via email at [email protected] .

item.title: National Ag Day in the Capital City celebrated with cow milking contest - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Special to Darkhorse Press
item.description:
JACKSON – Today, Commissioner of Agriculture and Commerce Andy Gipson and the Mississippi Department of Agriculture and Commerce celebrated National Ag Day with a focus on dairy including cow milking competitions and Genuine Mississippi milk and ice cream from the Beason Family Farm of Neshoba County. Governor Tate Reeves proclaimed today “Agriculture Day” in the State of Mississippi.

Commissioner Gipson was joined outside Galloway United Methodist Church, across from the Mississippi Capitol, by Mississippi farmers, legislators and local media representatives. State Representative Shanda Yates, State Representative Kent McCarty, State Senator Kamesha Mumford, State Senator Jeremy England, and various local media personalities all participated in the milking contests.

“Agriculture’s role in Mississippi has never been more important. It is the number one industry in the state, the backbone of our economy and the basis of our small towns and rural communities,” said Commissioner Gipson. “We are proud to take this time to recognize our farmers, ranchers and producers on this special day – National Agriculture Day. I encourage everyone to seek out and thank your local farmers today.”

Gipson went on to highlight the U.S. Dietary Guidelines released by the U.S. Department of Agriculture (USDA), the Mississippi Department of Agriculture and Commerce’s (MDAC) Make Mississippi Healthy Again initiative and MDAC’s Genuine MS® Program. He thanked Mississippi legislators for passing House Bill 1153 which prohibits the sale, offer for sale and the manufacture of “cell-cultured dairy products” that are derived from animal cells cultured outside of a live animal.

“We are living in a time where it seems everything is artificial, and you wonder what is real. We’ve seen everything from fake grass, astroturf, to fake meat, and now they’ve come up with lab grown, or fake, milk,” Commissioner Gipson continued. “So today, we’re especially proud to be here to celebrate agriculture, and to promote real food for real people. Thank you to our legislators for making Mississippi the first state in America to outlaw fake milk.”

Following brief remarks from Mississippi House Agriculture Committee Chairman Bill Pigott and Senate Agriculture Committee Chairman Neil Whaley, Commissioner Gipson invited the designated contestants to face off in back-to-back milking competitions with Jersey dairy cows provided by Beason Family Farm of Philadelphia. The Commissioner awarded first place trophies and bragging rights to the winners: Senator Jeremy England and Meteorologist Austin Powell, who collected the most milk within the time of two minutes. The cow milking contestants were encouraged by young people from the Galloway Children’s Center who chanted “milk that cow; milk that cow.”

Commissioner Gipson said, “Most of those children had not seen a cow in real life. None of them had seen a cow milked. Now they know where their milk and ice cream come from and they’ll remember this experience for years to come.”

Visitors and spectators were treated to fresh bottled milk and ice cream produced by the very cows on site and provided by Genuine MS® member Beason Family Farm.

View full Ag Day festivities at https://youtu.be/QL48OL5yWjo and the Ag Day proclamation signed by Governor Tate Reeves at https://agnet.mdac.ms.gov/agManage/uploads/3351.pdf .

“You are what you eat, and we are forever grateful to our farmers who grow and raise the food we consume every day,” said Gipson. “Another exciting initiative we are proud to take part in is the USDA’s national awareness campaign to highlight the ‘Product of USA’ label. This standard ensures that when consumers see the label on meat, poultry or processed egg products, it means the animal was born, raised, harvested and processed entirely within the United States. This labeling initiative to identify fresh, locally sourced food products raised right here in the U.S. not only supports our farmers, but also allows consumers to make informed, healthier decisions.”

Agriculture is the largest industry in the state of Mississippi, producing $9.5 billion in agricultural commodities last year alone. Agriculture also employs 11.4 percent of the state’s workforce and contributes to over 14 percent of the state’s overall economic activity. Mississippi currently ranks in the Top 20 in the U.S. for production of 11 agricultural commodities, including catfish, sweet potatoes, cotton, pine lumber, broilers, rice, peanuts and more.

National Ag Day was established in 1973 by the Agriculture Council of America as an effort to encourage every American to understand how food and fiber products are produced; appreciate the role agriculture plays in providing safe, abundant and affordable products; value the essential role of agriculture in maintaining a strong economy; and acknowledge and consider career opportunities in the agriculture, food and fiber industry. To learn more about National Agriculture Day, visit www.agday.org.

item.title: Mississippi DPS transfers 1960s Klan materials to state archives - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Morgan Howard
item.description:
JACKSON – The Mississippi Department of Public Safety has transferred a collection of 1960s-era Ku Klux Klan materials to the Mississippi Department of Archives and History after the items were recently discovered during preparations for a move to the agency’s new headquarters.

According to DPS, the materials include full Klan regalia and documents that were found inside a small blue suitcase. The inventory also contains charters, a spiral notebook with meeting minutes, a ledger book, a 1964 Imperial Executive Order and numerous pamphlets.

Officials said the collection includes Klan propaganda, including a pamphlet titled “The Ugly Truth about Martin Luther King,” published by United Klans of America.

The materials also include file folders containing news clippings about the Mississippi Highway Patrol, the Mississippi Department of Public Safety, former DPS Commissioner T.B. Birdsong and materials related to the Freedom Riders.

Mississippi Department of Public Safety Commissioner Sean Tindell said preserving the artifacts will help document the activities of hate groups and make sure future generations better understand that history.

The Mississippi Department of Archives and History said the transfer is significant because it gives researchers broader access to records that can deepen public understanding of Ku Klux Klan activity in Mississippi during the 1960s.

Incoming MDAH Director Barry White said the materials are especially notable because they include both administrative records and propaganda from a local chapter of a secretive national organization.

MDAH said all of the materials will be processed and eventually made digitally accessible to the public, though that work could take several months. The process will include arranging, housing and describing the collection, along with preparing a catalog overview, item-level finding aid and metadata for scanned images.

item.title: Meridian police investigate fatal shooting on 36th Avenue - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Greer Vari
item.description:
MERIDIAN – An adult male was found dead late Monday night following a reported shooting in Meridian.

Officers with the Meridian Police Department responded just after 10 p.m. on March 23 to reports of shots fired in the 1300 block of 36th Avenue. Upon arrival, officers located a man in a yard suffering from an apparent gunshot wound. He was pronounced dead at the scene.

The department’s Violent Crime Unit responded and is actively investigating the incident. The victim’s body will be transported to the Mississippi Crime Laboratory for an autopsy.

“This remains an active and ongoing investigation. We are asking anyone with information to come forward and assist us as we work to determine exactly what happened,” Assistant Chief Darrell Thompson said.

Authorities are asking anyone with information to contact the Meridian Police Department or Crime Stoppers as the investigation continues.

item.description:
GEORGE COUNTY – The George County Sheriff’s Office said deputies were involved in a vehicular pursuit that ended in the death of Austin McCraney.

In a statement, the sheriff’s office said the incident happened on the previous day, but no additional details were released.

The Mississippi Bureau of Investigation is now investigating the incident, according to the sheriff’s office. George County authorities said they will fully cooperate with the investigation.

Sheriff Mitchell Mixon said the department is committed to transparency and to cooperating fully as the Mississippi Bureau of Investigation conducts what he described as a thorough and independent review.

Additional information is expected to be released as it becomes available.
